$comment: resolutionRegistry.json -- NORMATIVE artifact of the EDUcore Enhanced Cockburn Use Case Standard v0.11 (identityResolutionContract-design-072826.md, Decision 2.2, as ratified 2026-07-29). One entry per citable standard; the entry KEY is the only legal value of a citation's `standard` field. `anchor` is `graph` (resolves against the DME standards graph via the universal stableId contract) or `document` (recognized standard, not graph-resolvable; Layer 4 verdicts document-anchored as a note, never a violation). A citation's `identifier` MUST be the target node's stableId, or match `shorthandPattern` and expand via `shorthandExpansion`. The registry is data, not code: adding a standard is an entry, not a release. A registry entry is a draft artifact until authorized through the human vetting step (ratification Q9). The registry is versionless by ruling (ratification Q7). Graph-source names verified against the DME golden (DmeStandardRoot) 2026-07-29.

CEDS.notes: P-prefix = property, C-prefix = class; bare six digits are ILLEGAL (ambiguous). Space forms like 'CEDS 000243' are ILLEGAL -- the standard belongs in the `standard` field, never inside the identifier.

PESC.notes: Cite the stableId curie directly (pesc:class/AcademicRecord/AcademicAwardType). No shorthand: PESC has no small native id.

OpenBadges.notes: Canonical DME source name for 1EdTech/IMS Open Badges v3.0 (verified 2026-07-29). Cite the stableId curie directly (openbadges:Achievement, openbadges:Achievement.achievementType). Prose forms like 'IMS OpenBadge v3p0 (...)' are not registry keys and do not conform.

W3C-VC.notes: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0. Recognized standard, not graph-resolvable: no DME source exists. Layer 4 verdicts citations against this entry `document-anchored` (warning-class note, never a violation).

W3C-DID.notes: W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0. Recognized standard, not graph-resolvable: no DME source exists. Layer 4 verdicts citations against this entry `document-anchored` (warning-class note, never a violation).
